successCriteria: I can describe the key features of Impressionism and Post-Impressionism

body.hook: In 1874, a group of painters rejected by the official Paris Salon held their own show. A critic mocked one painting, Monet's "Impression, Sunrise," and called them "Impressionists." The insult became the name of one of the most loved art movements in history.

vocabulary.definition: A group of artists sharing ideas and styles during a period.
A movement that captured light, colour and fleeting moments with visible brushstrokes.
Artists after Impressionism who used colour and form more expressively or structurally.
Painting outdoors, directly from the scene.
Placing strokes of pure colour side by side instead of blending.
The historical, social and technological setting of an artwork.

study.title: Capturing the Moment
study.question: How did Impressionism and Post-Impressionism respond to their times?
study.passage:
Context: In the mid-1800s, railways let artists reach the countryside, cities like Paris were modernizing, photography could record exact details, and portable tubes of paint (invented 1841) made outdoor painting easy.
Impressionism (about 1870s–1880s): Claude Monet, Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Berthe Morisot, Camille Pissarro. Features: painting outdoors, capturing changing light and weather, visible quick brushstrokes, broken colour, everyday modern subjects (cafés, train stations, leisure). Monet painted haystacks and Rouen Cathedral many times to show light at different hours.
Post-Impressionism (about 1886–1905): Vincent van Gogh (expressive swirling strokes and emotional colour), Paul Cézanne (structure, geometric forms, multiple viewpoints), Georges Seurat (pointillism, dots of colour based on colour science), Paul Gauguin (flat areas of symbolic colour).
Task: Compare one Impressionist and one Post-Impressionist painting using the organizer. Then explain how one change in society influenced the movement.

practice.q: Compare Impressionism and Post-Impressionism in one sentence.
practice.a: Impressionism captured light and moments; Post-Impressionism added emotion, structure or symbolism.

practice.q: How does a movement "respond to its time"?
practice.a: It reflects new technology, ideas and social change in its subjects and methods.
